subject: Snapshot archival schedule, restore rollback, and erase propagation latency
messages:
From: Erin Cole <erin.cole@greenbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: legal+compliance@greenbank.com
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Question: snapshot archival + erase propagation latency

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance team about how snapshot archival interacts with deletion requests:

- If a customer triggers a deletion on their primary dataset, how long before that tombstone/expunge is guaranteed to be removed from offsite/off-cluster snapshots?
- Do archived snapshots (cold storage) hold independent retention windows that could extend the presence of deleted records beyond the primary retention window?
- Do you have logs or an evidence file we can attach to our audit showing the propagation timeline for a sample deletion?

We're trying to confirm worst-case exposure time for GDPR erasure requests that touch long-tail snapshots. Any clarifications and an example timeline would be very helpful.

Thanks,
Erin Cole
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager
GreenBank Financial

P.S. We may need a short one-page statement for our audit pack if the answers are fairly definitive.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Erin Cole <erin.cole@greenbank.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-18T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: snapshot archival + erase propagation latency

Hi Erin —

Quick summary up front: primary deletion -> tombstone appears within seconds; regional tombstone propagation to hot replicas typically completes within minutes; archival (cold snapshots) is handled by scheduled snapshot sweeps and can retain deleted data for the remainder of the snapshot retention window unless explicit expunge/rollback is initiated. Worst-case presence on cold snapshots depends on when the snapshot was taken and the snapshot TTL.

Answers to your bullets:

- Guaranteed removal from offsite/off-cluster snapshots: we do not perform instant mutation of historical snapshots; instead we maintain an expunge pipeline. For deletions requested on Day 0, the expunge pipeline will mark the primary tombstone immediately and enqueue snapshot segments for expunge. The actual physical removal from archived snapshots occurs during the next archival-compact pass (we run a rolling archival compaction window every 7 days by default in the regions we serve). Because of that schedule, worst-case exposure on cold snapshots is up to ~7 days plus the time to complete the archival compaction job (typically under 48 hours after it begins). So safe worst-case: roughly 9 days from deletion request, unless an expedited expunge is performed.

- Independent retention windows: yes — snapshot retention/archival windows are independent metadata. If a snapshot that contains the record has a retention TTL of 90 days, the record remains in that snapshot until the snapshot is expired or compacted. The expunge pipeline can target snapshot segments and will remove data earlier than TTL if we perform an expunge job for compliance reasons (we've done this for customers under legal hold releases).

- Logs / evidence: attached is a small example extraction of our propagation logs for a sample deletion from 2026-10-15 showing tombstone creation, enqueue to expunge queue, and archival compaction marking. See "snapshot-propagation-log-20261015.txt". I've also included a machine-readable retention matrix mapping active retention windows to archival TTLs: "rbw_gb_retention_matrix.csv".

If GreenBank needs a one-page formal statement for audit, happy to draft with legal and compliance.

Notes / mitigation options if you want lower exposure windows:
- We can schedule expedited expunge jobs for specific accounts (typically requires a support runbook and a brief maintenance window).
- For Dedicated / Private deployments, customers can optionally reduce snapshot frequency or shorten archival TTLs via config to tradeoff shorter exposure with smaller recovery windows.
- We support on-demand snapshot purge for snapshots created after a deletion request (subject to sequence-numbering constraints).

I will loop in Jonas and Marissa to provide an ops runbook and the ETA for a targeted expedited expunge if you request it.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question: snapshot archival + erase propagation latency

Erin —

Adding a couple of operational clarifications:

1) Snapshot immutability semantics — our snapshot objects are immutable blobs; we do not rewrite historical snapshot files in place. Instead we write compaction manifests that exclude expunged sequence ranges. That means until compaction runs, the data bytes exist in the snapshot store but are logically inaccessible through the service API. For legal/audit purposes, the important metric is the time until the compaction manifest is published and the underlying storage provider confirms object lifecycle transition/expunge.

2) Expedited expunge flow — if GreenBank requests an expedited workflow we:
   - create a scoped expunge job for the account
   - run targeted compaction on affected snapshot segments (typically scoped by shard/date)
   - publish compaction manifests and run a storage lifecycle expunge request to the cloud provider

   Typical ETA for end-to-end expedited expunge (from request to storage-provider expunge confirmation) is 24–72 hours depending on object lifecycle schedules of the storage backend.

3) Evidence artifacts we can produce for audits:
   - Tombstone creation record (timestamp + sequence id)
   - Expunge queue entry / job id
   - Compaction manifest id and publish timestamp
   - Storage-provider expunge confirmation (where supported)

Marissa — can you attach an example compaction manifest and the sample evidence package we handed GreenBank earlier this year? Erin — I can prepare a short one-pager with the worst-case timeline and recommended mitigations for your audit.

Jonas
Director, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference
